text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Urban problems caused by unemployment, poverty and poor education are begining to emerge in some Finnish cities, ministry of environment report says.
- American man to be charged in Finnish court on Thursday for deliberately infecting several Finnish women with the HIV virus which causes AIDS.
- Government considers setting up a national award with a value of 200,000 to 500,000 markka for achievements in scientific research, says Prime minister Paavo Lipponen.
- Deportation orders are often carried out so quickly that the deported foreigners have no time to appeal, ombusdman Lauri Lehtimaija says.

- Finnish Export Credit to lose its monopoly in OECD credits to Finnish companies as another state-run company Fide Oy starts operating this year. Fide will even out interest rate expenses on up to six billion markka in credits in the next three years.
- Hackman's resigning CEO Curt Lindbom to become adviser for venture capital fund CapMan and has been called to join its board.
- Telecommunications group Nokia Oy does not plan to sell its 12 percent stake in unlisted commercial television MTV3, official says.

- Tamrock Construction -- part of Tampella which is due to change its name to Tamrock -- targets an increase in net sales to 1.5 billion markka from one billion. Current group net sales are 4.4 billion markka.
- Housholds to be able to take rivalling bids from electricity utilities from the start of 1998, officials say.
- Finland's roads are slippery and dangerous in the winter but there are not enough areas for off-road training on snow and ice, driving teachers say.

- A reduction of alcohol tax in Sweden which cut consumer prices of strong beer by over 20 percent at the turn of the year may compel Finland to a similar path, says Alko chief executive officer Reijo Salmi. Brewers demand tax cuts this year.

- Finance minister Sauli Niinisto says he is prepared to take the risks involved in lowering taxes more than earlier planned if there is a moderate wage settlement next autumn and the economy develops as forecast.
